stops.note: named the bark of the cinchona tree used to treat fevers
adopted by Spanish Jesuits who learned of the fever-bark remedy in Peru
coined by French chemists Pelletier and Caventou when they isolated the active alkaloid
stops.meaning: the isolated anti-malarial alkaloid from cinchona bark

stops.note: borrowed directly from the French scientific term
stops.meaning: a bitter compound used to treat malaria

current_meaning: a bitter alkaloid derived from cinchona bark, historically used to treat malaria and to flavor tonic water
